issue:
(bug): sqlglot corrupts PostgreSQL Unicode escape string literals (U&'...')

**Fully reproducible code snippet**
sqlglot misparses U& as identifier U + bitwise AND &, adding spaces during SQL regeneration.

Here is a snippet to test this behaviour:

```python
dialect = "postgres"
sql_original = """
    SELECT
        (U&'\FE01' || 'Test literal') AS label
    FROM data
"""
sql_transpiled = sqlglot.transpile(
    sql_original, read=dialect, write=dialect, pretty=True
)[0]

print(sql_transpiled)
```

Full output:

```
SyntaxWarning: "\F" is an invalid escape sequence. Such sequences will not work in the future. Did you mean "\\F"? A raw string is also an option.
  (U&'\FE01' || 'Test literal') AS label
SELECT
  (
    U & '\FE01' || 'Test literal'
  ) AS label
FROM data
```

**Official Documentation**
PostgreSQL [documentation](https://www.postgresql.org/docs/current/sql-syntax-lexical.html#:~:text=A%20variant%20of%20quoted%20identifiers%20allows%20including%20escaped%20Unicode%20characters%20identified%20by%20their%20code%20points%2E) part about escaped Unicode characters in string literals.

> This variant starts with U& (upper or lower case U followed by ampersand) immediately before the opening double quote, without any spaces in between, for example U&"foo". (Note that this creates an ambiguity with the operator &. Use spaces around the operator to avoid this problem.) Inside the quotes, Unicode characters can be specified in escaped form by writing a backslash followed by the four-digit hexadecimal code point number or alternatively a backslash followed by a plus sign followed by a six-digit hexadecimal code point number. For example, the identifier "data" could be written as `U&"d\0061t\+000061"`
